families.admitted_normalized_statement: For every positive dimension n, a full-dimensional compact convex body K in real n-space with barycenter zero and with zero as its only interior lattice point has ordinary Euclidean volume at most (n+1)^n/n!. The bound is attained by the translated dilation (n+1)Delta_n-(1,...,1). No classification of all equality cases is asserted.

current_revision_findings.scope_exclusion_preserved: The current text still states that classification of all equality cases is not determined.

families.admitted_normalized_statement: There exists a finite nonempty family F of connected bipartite finite simple graphs, every member containing a cycle, such that ex(n,F)=O(n^(4/3-1/48)) while for every member H of F one has ex(n,H)=Omega(n^(4/3)). Consequently no member controls the family extremal number up to a constant factor, so the corrected Erdos-Simonovits compactness conjecture fails.

There exist a fixed finite connected bipartite 2-degenerate graph H and positive real constants c and epsilon such that ex(n,H) is at least c*n^(3/2+epsilon) for all sufficiently large natural n. This refutes the conjectured O(n^(3/2)) bound for fixed bipartite 2-degenerate graphs and hence the r=2 case of the general degeneracy conjecture.
